lessons.lesson: Anchor stop prices to the expected fill, not the last reference close, whenever a name has gapped or is reacting to news. Check that the stated stop distance (e.g. 10%) still holds at the likely entry price before approving.
evidence: 2026-10-20 DPZ: stop of $274.88 was set 10% under the $305.42 reference close, but the buy filled at $316.58 (about 3.7% higher), so the stop sat about 13% below entry instead of the intended 10%.

2026-10-26 DPZ: the held position's invalidation ($274.88) is still anchored to the pre-fill reference close and sits about 13% below the $316.58 fill; the PM review flags it as unfixed. Re-anchor existing theses to the actual fill when reviewing held positions.

lessons.lesson: Never write 'no earnings event in the window' just because the news note doesn't mention a name. Check the name's own earnings estimate and recent 8-K 2.02 / 10-Q filings in the inputs, and say 'unverified' only if they are truly absent. The News Analyst should cover every symbol on the proposal menu, not only flagged ones, so the Portfolio Manager does not shrink positions for lack of data.

EQT to acquire Range Resources in an all-stock deal valuing one RRC share at 0.987 EQT shares, pro forma EV over $50B (8-K items 1.01, 7.01, 8.01, 9.01 filed 10-26): A transformative deal that overrides earnings and ordinary fundamentals for RRC. The price now tracks EQT, and the gap to the implied value reflects deal-completion risk (regulatory review, shareholder votes). The mega-merger framing adds a read-through to other gas names (GPOR, LNG indirectly). It also resolves the stale-earnings question as secondary, though the 10-28 results may still come.

Apple unveils redesigned iPad mini with 8.5-inch OLED, A20 Pro chip; iPhone Duo sells out amid long delays; Jefferies (Sell) raises PT to $270.62: Product momentum is positive ahead of the Oct 28 event and the 10-29 or 11-02 print, and the Duo demand evidence is the strongest in the thread. Offsets: cautious sell-side from last week (Loop, MoffettNathanson), Thiel's critique (opinion), and Omdia's 20% y/y smartphone shipment decline. Headlines tagged AAPL about AI bubbles and breadth are market commentary, not Apple news; ignore them.

Instacart exploring a sale with preliminary talks with Uber and DoorDash (The Information, 10-23); halts differential pricing experiments (10-26): Takeover speculation from a single press source, unconfirmed, plus a regulatory concession on algorithmic pricing that echoes the shelf-label scrutiny on grocers (KR). Both are headline and deal risk for CART ahead of 11-09 earnings.

DA Davidson lowers Domino's PT to $382 from $423, maintains Buy: A roughly 10% target cut is the first notable sell-side move on DPZ since the 10-20 buy. The rating is unchanged, so this reads as valuation or estimate trimming rather than a thesis break.

Pomerantz LLP investigates securities fraud claims against Mueller Industries after Q3 results: Plaintiff-firm solicitations follow most stock drops and are weak evidence of wrongdoing. It continues the 10-20 print story (EPS miss, revenue beat) and matters only if a class action or an 8-K follows.
Wedbush raises VeriSign PT to $367 from $351, Outperform: Post-earnings follow-through after Citi's $345 on 10-23; supportive, but the print is already known and this adds no new fact.
Citigroup lowers BJ's Restaurants PT to $70 from $75, Neutral: A small cut three trading days before the estimated 10-29 print, in line with a cautious restaurant sector; the print is the real risk.

Incyte to co-fund Genmab's Phase 1/2 study of petosemtamab combination in first-line KRAS G12D colorectal cancer: Early-stage pipeline collaboration, modest cash cost and long-dated payoff; it does not change the picture ahead of the likely 10-27 print.

RBC, UBS and Deutsche adjust Boston Beer PTs after Q3; RBC says volume growth remains weak despite margin gains: Continues the 10-23 story of a volume guidance cut offset by a raised EPS floor. The sell side is split and confirms volume as the weak spot.

Walmart announces three holiday shopping events from Nov 12 to Dec 2: Routine seasonal marketing, not material. The constructive sell-side thread continues, but stretched momentum is the more relevant caution; the 10-23 8.01 filing is still unread.

Retailers, including Kroger, face scrutiny over electronic shelf labels and dynamic pricing (MarketWatch, 10-24): A sector-wide regulatory theme that echoes the $5B price investment and the CART pricing retreat; no Kroger-specific action yet.

El-Erian warns of $150 oil if the Iran conflict widens; Burry backs Griffin on AI bubble and GPU overcapacity; futures higher after Trump rules out an immediate Iran strike: Relief in futures this morning against a two-sided macro setup. Oil is the swing factor for the Fed meeting, mega-cap earnings and the AI-capex thread that dominated 10-20 to 10-23.

Bitcoin drops to $80,000; Bilello: Bitcoin and gold are 2026's two worst-performing major assets: Continues the slide from the failed $84.3k breakout. Bears now cite $72k to $76k, and gold's break below $4,000 shows a broad lack of haven demand. No regulatory or exchange shock, so this is price action plus macro (Fed, Iran). Bullish bets (Alfred, Novogratz) are opinion.

Gold falls below $4,000 as yields rise ahead of the FOMC; extreme oversold and short data: A 15% drawdown from the 8-25 peak with positioning stretched to the downside. A bounce is plausible, but the Fed decision is the next catalyst.

note: Lessons come from a handful of trades; treat each as a hypothesis with the evidence it cites, not a rule. Hard limits are in code and lessons can't change them.
